ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text:
A thin-walled, thermally conductive cylindrical container with mass $m$ and smooth inner walls encloses a certain amount of ideal gas with a piston of cross-sectional area $S$. In all the following processes, the cylinder does not leak and remains in contact with the piston. When the cylinder is placed vertically inverted as shown in figure (a), the gas volume inside the cylinder is $V_{1}$, and the temperature is $T_{1}$. Given the magnitude of gravitational acceleration as $g$, and the atmospheric pressure as $p_{0}$.

1. The cylinder is suspended vertically as shown in figure (b), and the gas temperature inside the cylinder remains $T_{1}$. Determine the gas volume $V_{2}$ inside the cylinder at this state.
2. As shown in figure (c), the cylinder is placed horizontally. After equilibrium, the cylinder is slowly heated. When the gas volume inside the cylinder is $V_{3}$, calculate the temperature of the gas inside the cylinder at this state.

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The attached figure contains three schematic diagrams. In (a), the container has an inverted shape with its opening downward, the piston is placed horizontally, the piston rod is supported on the ground, and the gas is between the piston and the inner wall of the upper end of the container; the horizontal outer surface of the upper end of the container is subjected to atmospheric pressure, and the inner horizontal surface is subjected to gas pressure. In (b), the container is placed vertically and suspended from above, the bottom of the container is below, the piston is horizontally located at the upper part, and the gas is inside the container below the piston; the outside of the bottom of the container is acted on upward by atmospheric pressure, and the inside of the bottom is acted on downward by gas pressure. In (c), the container is placed horizontally on the ground, the piston is a vertical surface and can move along the horizontal direction, the weight of the container is supported by the ground, and in the horizontal direction one side of the piston is subjected to gas pressure and the other side is subjected to atmospheric pressure. Reasoning: Let the gas pressure in state (a) be p1. For the container in (a), make vertical force balance: the force of the gas on the inner wall of the upper end of the container is upward, with magnitude p1 S; the force of the atmosphere on the outer wall of the upper end of the container is downward, with magnitude p0 S; the weight of the container mg is downward. Therefore p1 S = p0 S + mg, giving p1 = (p0 S + mg)/S. Let the gas pressure in state (b) be p2. For the container in (b), make vertical force balance: the force of the atmosphere on the outside of the bottom of the container is upward, with magnitude p0 S; the force of the gas on the inside of the bottom of the container is downward, with magnitude p2 S; the weight of the container mg is downward. Therefore p0 S = p2 S + mg, giving p2 = (p0 S - mg)/S. From (a) to (b), the amount of gas substance is unchanged, and the temperatures are both T1, so by the ideal gas equation of state there is p1 V1 = p2 V2. Substituting p1 and p2 gives V2 = [(p0 S + mg)/(p0 S - mg)] V1. In (c), the container is placed horizontally, and the weight is supported by the ground, not affecting the axial equilibrium of the piston; when the piston is in equilibrium along the horizontal direction, the gas pressure equals the atmospheric pressure p0. From the initial state (a), one can obtain nR = p1 V1/T1 = [(p0 S + mg)V1]/(S T1). When the gas volume in (c) is V3 and the temperature is T, p0 V3 = nR T. Solving gives T = p0 V3 / nR = [p0 S V3 T1]/[(p0 S + mg)V1].
